correctness.rationale: A finite-trace Gaussian covariance operator and bounded multiplication yield a self-adjoint trace-class Gaussian quadratic kernel. Its Fredholm characteristic determinant yields an everywhere nonzero modulus. For one-sign modulation the positive kernel increases in Loewner order and all eigenvalues increase by min-max, proving complete-positive divisibility of invertible phase-damping maps. If modulation has both signs, absolute primitive cannot be monotone; a static Gaussian produces a strict modulus revival, which extends by finite-horizon Gaussian OU L2 continuity to finite nonzero relaxation rate. All quantifiers, boundaries, phase and sign conventions are explicit. Independent finite-dimensional checks: 480 monotonic comparisons, 18 finite-correlation echo/static checks and 20 determinant checks.

originality.rationale: The 2024 Cai et al. paper derives dephasing for specific OU and telegraph bath configurations, not a sharp if-and-only-if condition under arbitrary sign-varying deterministic modulation for all continuous Gaussian covariance kernels. Cywiński 2013 studies pulsed control of quadratic Gaussian dephasing and gives cumulant resummations but does not state the universal bath-quantified CP-divisibility classification or necessity with finite-memory stationary OU. Norris et al. 2015 studies non-Gaussian bath spectroscopy rather than an all-baths CP-divisibility dichotomy. Standard determinant, min–max and dephasing-channel criteria are conceded. Closest semantic published-finding corpus matches concern random-telegraph frozen discord, Holstein bath approximation error, and bang-control sampling, which do not imply the new classification. A broad unpublished/undiscovered universal theorem remains a plausible risk; priority cannot be established definitively.
residual_risks: The Fredholm determinant and monotone eigenvalue argument are established machinery; a broad prior theorem not captured by searches may subsume the physical classification.
The status is self-review only; independent review and exhaustive publication-priority verification are not performed.

value.rationale: Whether a noisy phase-damping qubit is CP-divisible for every admissible bath is a structural control-robustness question, not a chosen-parameter computation. The theorem classifies all bounded modulation profiles and every continuous centered Gaussian covariance, proves the sharp converse using physically mixing finite-memory OU noise, and distinguishes uniform protection from bath-specific suppression or echo. It gives a natural design boundary for nonlinear Gaussian-dephasing control and interpretation of information-backflow witnesses; no downstream theorem is presumed.
